chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, all of them, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of Dhuhr and 'Asr, so he said: 'When the sun departs (from its zenith), Dhuhr enters, and 'Asr enters together with it, except that this (Dhuhr) is before this ('Asr). Then you are in the time of both of them together until the sun sets.'

key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْس: Departure of the sun from its zenith (noon)

ai.seo_question: What is the exact time for Dhuhr and Asr prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the continuous window for Dhuhr and 'Asr, emphasizing that while Dhuhr precedes 'Asr, both share the same temporal boundary from solar zenith to sunset. This establishes the flexibility (tawassu') in prayer timing, allowing believers to perform either prayer within this extended period, a key principle in Shia fiqh for managing congregational or individual worship.
